title: A bigger test charge
hook: Change test charge magnitude and predict electric-force magnitude.
misconception: electric-force magnitude stays fixed when test charge magnitude doubles.
objective: Apply F = abs(q)E to compare electric-force magnitude when test charge magnitude changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a fixed external electric field, F = abs(q)E. When test charge magnitude doubles, electric-force magnitude becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model F = abs(q)E; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a fixed external electric field, with a nonzero initial result. If test charge magnitude triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on electric-force magnitude?
recall.why: Apply F = abs(q)E under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
